original_question: Is one of the subunits of the electron-transferring flavoprotein, which is mutated in individuals with glutaric acidemia type 2, encoded by a gene localized on chromosome 19?
key_entities: glutaric acidemia type 2, encoded by a gene localized on chromosome 19?

final_qi.question: Is one of the subunits of the electron-transferring flavoprotein, which is mutated in individuals with glutaric acidemia type 2, encoded by a gene localized on chromosome 19?
final_qi.long_answer: Electron-transferring flavoprotein (ETF) is a mitochondrial heterodimer composed of an α-subunit and a β-subunit. Mutations in either subunit cause multiple-acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency, also called glutaric acidemia type II. The gene for the ETF β-subunit (ETFB) has been mapped cytogenetically to chromosome 19q13.3, whereas the α-subunit gene (ETFA) is on chromosome 15q24-q25. Because the β-subunit gene is indeed located on chromosome 19, the statement that one of the ETF subunits mutated in glutaric acidemia type II is encoded by a gene on chromosome 19 is correct.
